newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - CNA Gallo year share seen flat.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - CNA Gallo year share seen flat.

text.p: A continued slump in consumer spending triggered by high interest rates would likely hold CNA Gallo's year-end profits steady, a consensus poll of analysts showed on Wednesday.
The South African leisure firm and retailer's earnings per share would be more or less flat, dipping by a slight two percent on the previous year, when it reports next Tuesday.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast a consensus earnings per share figure of 25.3 cents from 25.8 cents within a range of 24.5 cents to 26.8 cents.
They forecast a dividend of 10.7 cents from 10.5 cents within a range of 10.5 cents and 11.1 cents.

"Until they (interest rates) are cut it's going to be very, very tough out there for people relying on people's disposable income," Natasha Ingham of the Johannesburg-based stockbroking firm Standard Equities told Reuters.
"It's not just CNA, it's all the clothing retailers and everyone selling on credit. CNA is very closely related to consumer spending," Ingham added.
Her forecast was less optimistic than that of other analysts. "I am expecting their earnings to be down five percent," Ingham said.

Analysts who forecast a small rise in CNA's earnings said they based their expectations on the company's software and multimedia operation Nuware as well as its recent alliance with Sweets from Heaven.
"Nuware is doing very well, it's a very good concept and Sweets from Heaven stores are going to do very well," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

Sweets from Heaven made a deal with CNA in January under which it would franchise its outlets in CNA branches and Nu Metro cinema complexes throughout the country. CNA has a 25 percent stake in the sweets firm.
Analysts said an interest rate cut could occur in the last quarter of this year, helping CNA recover lost ground during the first half of 1998.
"We are thinking that if we had an interest rate cut it will probably be in the final quarter of the year, so it's another six months for CNA," one analyst said.
Should it report disappointing results, CNA will be no different from other key retail companies.
Recent corporate results from South African Breweries Ltd, food and pharmaceutical firm Tiger Oats Ltd and CG Smith Foods Ltd have let the market down.
"People haven't got money to spend on discretionary items," said an analyst.

CNA's announcement last week that it was considering a restructuring to more effectively capitalise on opportunities for growth of its entertainment and leisure activities was received positively by the market.
Commentators said a restructuring would enable the group to better reap the benefits from all its operations.

CNA Gallo is a diverse holding and investment company with interests in specialists book stores, music software manufacturing and distribution, stationary products, film and video distribution and cinema.
